title: Launch baton playbook and content-freeze flow for coordinated blog/email/social/webinar
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a single-source 'baton' playbook that sequences content production, approvals, and channel handoffs for an integrated announcement (blog, marketing email, social, webinar). Goal: reduce last-minute changes, enforce a predictable content-freeze, and provide a clear on-call/owner matrix for the 72 hours around launch.
scope: Define content owners, backups, and SLAs for blog/email/social/webinar
Establish content-freeze gates and staging artifacts (final drafts, assets, alt text)
Author release-notes coordination template with API/SDK changelog sections
Create a timeline with hard milestones and a 72-hour launch playbook
Provide monitoring and rollback triggers for marketing/console pages
out_of_scope: Detailed creative design work (assets will be owned by Design team tickets)
Paid advertising buys and media placements
Post-launch deep analytics playbook (will link to Analytics team runbook)
channel_matrix: Blog - Owner: Content (Maya Rivera); Final draft due: 2026-04-06; Asset deliverables: hero image, OG image, embedded demo GIF; Drive: https://drive.redwood/content/blog-launch-v1

Marketing Email - Owner: Growth (Devon Park); Send window: 2026-04-15 10:00 PT; Requirements: short intro, feature bullets, CTA to docs + webinar signup; Email doc: https://drive.redwood/marketing/email-launch
Social - Owner: Brand (Eleanor Cho); Cadence: 3 posts across Twitter/X, LinkedIn, and Mastodon within first 24h; Assets: GIF + 2 text variants; Slack channel: #announce-social
Webinar - Owner: Solutions (Arjun Malik); Date/Time: 2026-04-16 09:00 PT; Runbook: https://drive.redwood/webinar/runbooks/launch-2026
Release Notes - Owner: Developer Relations (Samira Gomez); Structured sections: breaking changes, upgrade notes, examples, SDK snippets; Template: https://drive.redwood/devrel/release-notes-template

content_freeze_policy: Soft freeze at 2026-04-01: no major content pivots; PRs accepted for copy only
Hard freeze at 2026-04-06 23:59 PT: only critical fixes allowed; all fixes require PM approval and changelog entry
Freeze exceptions: security fixes, legal copy changes, and critical SDK/compatibility updates
Process for exceptions: owner opens a Freeze Exception ticket, documents justification, and PM signs off in Slack thread #launch-baton
release_notes_coordination: DevRel publishes a structured release-notes draft by 2026-03-20 including migration steps and code snippets
Engineering owners add SDK changelog entries and link PRs (GitHub PRs must be referenced in the release notes) - Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/6342
PM reviews release notes for customer-facing language and ensures feature mapping to marketing bullets
Docs publishing: docs site staging link will be created and smoke-tested by eng on 2026-04-10
Final release notes live at publish window and embedded in blog and support articles
pre_launch_checklist: All channel owners have sign-off in the shared spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood/launch-baton
Assets uploaded to Drive and accessible to public links for press kit
Monitoring dashboards live: console latencies, API errors, signups - Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/launch-2026
Contact list (internal + press) validated and distribution lists tested
Rollback criteria documented and tested (e.g., disable banner, retract email in ESP)
post_launch_actions: 72-hour active monitoring window with on-call rotation and dedicated Slack channel #launch-ops
Collect initial metrics at 1h, 6h, 24h, 72h windows and post into the launch doc
Triaging feedback: route product issues to Eng alpha channel, comms issues to Content/Brand
Schedule retrospective on 2026-04-20 and publish a short postmortem and learnings
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Late copy changes slip past content freeze - Mitigation: PM approval gate + snapshot of artifacts in Drive
Risk: Docs/SDK mismatch causes developer confusion - Mitigation: require engineers to sign off on release-note snippets and include example code in tests
Risk: Webinar no-shows - Mitigation: record run-through and promote on socials; have on-demand recording available
Risk: High traffic causing console latency - Mitigation: pre-warm caches, enable fallback routes, and coordinate with infra ops
